openhuman-tui is a conversation-first ratatui frontend

label: OpenBot frames a bot as eight primitives in four pairs; Conversations is how work is given and Activity is what the bot did, in a fixed order.

OpenBot supports several bots in one conversation through a server-owned shared transcript: @Name addresses one bot, otherwise every addressed bot runs through the headless AG-UI path and answers in its own attributed thread.
OpenBot's activity pane is a typed lifecycle view (routine, responsibility, handoff and related kinds) with icons and links back to the producing routine, task or conversation.
OpenBot Desktop is a Tauri 2 shell responsible for the machine around the bot: tray, engine and stack install, updates, host folder access, telemetry, recorder and uninstall.

openhuman ships openhuman-tui, a conversation-first ratatui and crossterm terminal frontend embedding the core in-process, covering login, saved conversations, model and agent selection, approvals, tools and diagnostics.

openhuman-tui is a first-class host: it consumes the same web_chat broadcast stream as the desktop app and exposes /sessions, /permissions, /skills and /mcp as commands, with a persistent attention control for pending approvals.
The other reference repos split between Electron (OpenMausBot, OpenGhost), Tauri (buzz), a Hermes dashboard plugin (hermes-muse) and web/api workspaces (rakazo, turnstone).

Skilled bots has no conversation surface today: the bots CLI exposes run, inbox, enqueue, drain, answer and status; answer continues a needs-you item and status reports last run, delivery and open items from the status index.

A TUI can carry conversations, approvals, activity and routines because all four are text-first and event-driven; a Tauri shell adds a native window and tray, self-update, OS folder authority, microphone capture and engine supervision that a small team does not need on day one.
